# frozen_string_literal: true

# Resolves and verifies a Ruby development toolchain from repository
# evidence, following the evidence-first procedure: inspect what the
# repository declares, observe what the local runtime actually provides,
# and only then act. The declared requirement and the observed runtime
# are resolved separately so a mismatch is reported as a conflict instead
# of being silently absorbed; executable provenance is verified so ruby
# and bundle come from one installation before Bundler installs anything;
# and a native-extension failure is classified from concrete build output
# so the missing prerequisite is named instead of working around it by
# weakening the runtime requirement.
class RubyToolchainAdvisor
  # Compares the declared requirement with the observed runtime and the
  # resolved executables. Status is "conflict" when ruby and bundle
  # resolve from different installations, when the observed runtime does
  # not satisfy the declared requirement, or when either version cannot
  # be parsed into segments.
  def resolve(declared_ruby:, observed_ruby:, ruby_executable:, bundle_executable:)
    {
      "status" => resolution_status(
        declared_ruby: declared_ruby,
        observed_ruby: observed_ruby,
        ruby_executable: ruby_executable,
        bundle_executable: bundle_executable
      ),
      "declared_ruby" => declared_ruby,
      "observed_ruby" => observed_ruby,
      "ruby_executable" => ruby_executable,
      "bundle_executable" => bundle_executable
    }
  end

  # Application dependencies are installed through Bundler so the Gemfile
  # stays the single dependency contract and no global gems are mixed in.
  # With a lockfile, bundle check reports drift before bundle install
  # reconciles it; without one, bundle install resolves and writes it.
  def dependency_command(lockfile_present:)
    lockfile_present ? "bundle check && bundle install" : "bundle install"
  end

  # Classifies a native-extension build failure from the concrete
  # compiler, linker, or make output so the correct prerequisite is
  # fixed rather than the runtime version.
  def native_extension_classification(error_output)
    output = error_output.to_s
    if output.include?("ruby.h")
      "missing-ruby-header"
    elsif output.include?("ld:") || output.include?("library not found")
      "linker"
    elsif output.include?("make") && output.include?("not found")
      "missing-build-tool"
    else
      "unclassified"
    end
  end

  # The declared runtime is repository evidence. Installation failures
  # are resolved at the toolchain level (headers, linker libraries,
  # build tools); the requirement itself is never relaxed to make the
  # failure disappear.
  def runtime_change_allowed?(reason:)
    # Every reported reason (for example: #{reason}) is a toolchain
    # problem to diagnose, never a justification to change the runtime.
    false
  end

  private

  def resolution_status(declared_ruby:, observed_ruby:, ruby_executable:, bundle_executable:)
    return "conflict" unless same_installation?(ruby_executable, bundle_executable)
    return "conflict" unless requirement_satisfied?(declared_ruby, observed_ruby)

    "supported"
  end

  def same_installation?(ruby_executable, bundle_executable)
    File.dirname(ruby_executable) == File.dirname(bundle_executable)
  end

  # Segment-wise comparison so "3.3" is satisfied by "3.3.6" but not by
  # "3.2.4", and "3.1" is not satisfied by "3.10.0" (one differs from
  # ten). An unparsable or partially-specified observed version cannot
  # confirm the requirement, so it conflicts conservatively.
  def requirement_satisfied?(declared, observed)
    declared_segments = version_segments(declared)
    observed_segments = version_segments(observed)
    return false if declared_segments.nil? || observed_segments.nil?
    return false if declared_segments.length > observed_segments.length

    declared_segments.zip(observed_segments).all? { |declared_value, observed_value| declared_value == observed_value }
  end

  def version_segments(version)
    version.to_s.split(".").map { |segment| Integer(segment, 10) }
  rescue ArgumentError, TypeError
    nil
  end
end
